title: Adaptive Cost Safety Net & Heterogeneous GPU Routing
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Implement a runtime safety net that enforces per-customer and per-route spend limits while making smart routing decisions across heterogeneous GPU pools (spot vs on-demand and different SKUs). The feature should: 1) Predict short-term spend trajectory for active workloads, 2) Apply soft and hard budget caps with configurable grace behavior, 3) Select the most cost-efficient GPU SKU (e.g., T4, A10, A100) given latency SLOs and model variant compatibility, and 4) Gracefully degrade to fallback model variants when spend caps are hit or capacity is constrained. This ticket prototypes the policy engine, runtime hooks for re-routing, and a canary config for 10 customers in staging.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can compute per-customer projected spend for next 10 minutes with <= 10% error based on historical token distribution and current QPS
Policy engine supports soft cap (throttle + warning) and hard cap (reject or fallback) per-route and per-customer
Routing decision selects GPU SKU that meets latency SLO >= 90th percentile for the route while minimizing expected cost given current spot prices
When hard cap reached, system automatically routes to preconfigured fallback model variant (quantized or smaller) within 500ms decision latency
Metrics exposed to Console: projected burn rate, cap state (OK/WARN/HARD), last routing decision with reason, and re-route latency
Integration tests covering spot price spike scenarios, GPU preemption simulation, and simultaneous hard-cap enforcement across two routes
implementation_notes: Architecture: add Cost Safety Net component in router that subscribes to (1) pricing feed (spot/on-demand), (2) capacity signals from scheduler, and (3) per-customer quota state. The component outputs a routing decision: preferred_pool -> fallback_variant -> action (serve/queue/reject). Use a lightweight in-memory projection (exponential smoothing of token burn) and a budget policy DSL for soft/hard thresholds. Persist policy state to Redis for fast access and to Postgres for audit logs. Key trade-offs: aggressive projections reduce overspend but can over-throttle bursty traffic; choose conservative smoothing constant for first canary. Avoid large synchronous calls in hot path; use cached decisions with 1s TTL.
risks: 1) Incorrect spend projections could cause false hard-caps and customer impact. 2) Routing instability if spot price feed flaps; need hysteresis and min-route-duration. 3) Fallback model variants may not preserve output quality; require eval gating. 4) Additional latency from policy decision must remain below 10ms median to not impact SLOs.
test_plan: Unit tests for projection module and policy DSL
Integration test in staging simulating spot price surge and node preemption (kube evict)
Load test with synthetic customer profiles exercising per-route caps and fallback routing
Canary rollout: 10 customers with controlled budgets for 72 hours, monitor error rates and cost delta
Post-mortem checklist if canary triggers unexpected hard-caps
